verb
give back something you borrowed, or give work to a teacher (AmE)
typical: turn sth in. NOT for: keeping.
Turn in your homework on Monday.
She turned in her essay.
verb
go to bed (informal)
typical: turn in (for the night). NOT for: staying up.
I'm tired; I'll turn in.
We turned in at ten.
verb
tell the police about someone who has committed a crime
typical: turn sb in. NOT for: protecting.
His brother turned him in.
She turned herself in.
turn into: verb
become something different, or make someone or something become different
typical: turn into + noun, turn sb/sth into sth. NOT for: staying the same.
The sofa turns into a bed.
Hollywood turned her into a star.
verb
change by magic from one thing into another
typical: turn sb/sth into sth. NOT for: staying the same.
In a flash, the prince turned into a frog.
The witch turned them all into stone.
verb
used to say that a long time has passed (days into weeks, months into years)
typical: days turn into weeks. NOT for: short time.
Days turned into weeks and still there was no news.
Months turned into years.
verb
develop into something, often unexpectedly
typical: sth turns into sth. NOT for: ending.
The discussion turned into an argument.
The small shop turned into a big business.
turn off: verb
make a machine or light stop working
typical: turn off the TV/engine/lights. NOT for: turning on.
Turn the lights off when you leave.
He turned off the engine.
verb
stop water or gas from flowing by turning a tap or handle
typical: turn the water/gas off. NOT for: turning on.
They turned the gas off for a few hours.
Turn off the tap.
verb
leave the road you are on to take another
typical: turn off (at) the motorway/exit. NOT for: going straight on.
We should have turned off at the last exit.
She turned off the highway.
verb
make someone dislike something
typical: turn sb off (sth). NOT for: attracting.
The sight of the dirt turned me off.
Long speeches turn people off.
turn on: make a machine or light start working by pressing a button
typical: turn sth on. NOT for: turning off.
make water or gas start flowing
typical: turn sth on (a tap). NOT for: turning off.
suddenly attack or criticize someone you were friendly to
typical: turn on sb. NOT for: protecting.
The dog turned on its owner.
typical: turn on sth. NOT for: being independent.
The case turns on one question.
turn out: verb
happen in a particular way, or prove to be something
typical: turn out well/badly, it turns out that, turn out to be sth. NOT for: switching off lights.
Things turned out all right in the end.
He turned out to be her cousin.
verb
switch off a light
typical: turn out the light(s). NOT for: going out for an event.
Don't forget to turn out the lights.
She turned the lamp out and went to sleep.
verb
go to an event as part of a crowd
typical: people turn out for an election/match. NOT for: producing goods.
About 70% of voters turned out for the election.
Thousands turned out to watch the parade.
verb
force someone to leave a place, especially their home
typical: turn sb out (of sth). NOT for: leaving by choice.
They turned the family out onto the street.
If you cannot pay the rent, they will turn you out.
turn over: verb
give someone the right to own or manage something
typical: turn sth over to sb. NOT for: taking control.
He'll turn the shop over to his son.
I'm turning the project over to you.
verb
use land or a building for a different purpose
typical: turn sth over to sth. NOT for: keeping it the same.
The land was turned over to farming.
The old school was turned over to housing.
verb
take a criminal to the police
typical: turn sb over to the police. NOT for: letting someone go.
The thief was turned over to the police.
They turned him over to the law.
verb
turn a page or flip something to the other side (BrE)
typical: turn over the page/a card. NOT for: turning off.
Turn over and look at the next page.
Turn the meat over after five minutes.
turn to: verb
try to get help, advice or sympathy from someone
typical: turn to sb. NOT for: avoiding.
I don't know who to turn to.
She turned to her parents for help.
verb
start doing or using something new, as a way of solving a problem
typical: turn to sth. NOT for: avoiding.
Many people are turning to solar power.
He turned to drink.
verb
find a page in a book
typical: turn to page + number. NOT for: closing.
Turn to page 25.
Please turn to the next exercise.
verb
change into something else
typical: turn to stone/dust. NOT for: staying the same.
The water turned to ice.
The wood turned to dust.
turn up: verb
increase heat, sound or power with a switch
typical: turn the volume/heating/oven up, turn sth up. NOT for: reducing.
Turn the oven up to 220.
Turn up the radio, I love this song!
verb
be found, especially by chance after being lost
typical: a lost item turns up. NOT for: finding it by searching.
My watch turned up in a coat pocket.
Don't worry, your keys will turn up.
verb
arrive, especially unexpectedly or late
typical: turn up late/early/on time. NOT for: going away.
You can't just turn up and expect a meal.
Steve turned up late, as usual.
verb
happen unexpectedly, used about an opportunity or situation
typical: a job/chance/opportunity turns up. NOT for: people arriving.
I'm sure a job will turn up soon.
Something always turns up.
type up: type a text from notes or a handwritten draft
typical: type sth up. NOT for: handwriting.
I need to type up my notes.
